title: Can Probing Classifiers Detect Incorrect Future Tokens Before the Model 'Commits' to Them? An Early-Warning Experiment

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tight causal chain: if incorrect/harmful tokens can be detected in intermediate layers before generation, this enables pre-emptive runtime safety interventions. This is a direct, actionable safety application of interpretability with clear deployment implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Probing classifiers on residual streams are standard TransformerLens/ARENA workflows. Creating a correct/incorrect completion dataset requires some care. Training probes per layer is methodologically clear. Medium compute is sufficient for a 7B model.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: detection accuracy by layer for correct vs incorrect completions. Dataset construction, probe training across layers, and comparison with/without planning circuit knowledge is multi-step. Tight in 30 hours but achievable with a focused factual-recall task.
